title: Siegard hook declaration
description: Contract for src/claude/hooks/hooks.declaration.json, the authored source the generator turns into the distribution's hooks/hooks.json. specs/0010 R10 requires a hook to state the event it binds, the matcher that selects it, the single guarantee it enforces, and the reason it emits on denial; R11 requires it to state its own timeout rather than inherit the 600-second default. Those facts have to live somewhere authored and checkable, and a registry inside the generator would be a rule that only a script could see. This file is source-only: the generator reads it and never ships it, because a consumer reads hooks/hooks.json and specs/0008 R7 closes the directory set to what the harness or Siegard actually loads.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects a declaration it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

hooks.description: One entry per shipped hook. An empty declaration would ship an empty hooks/ directory, which specs/0008 R7 omits rather than installs.

file.description: The hook script, resolved relative to src/claude/hooks/ in source and to ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/ once installed.

event.description: specs/0010 R12: a hook binds an event the documentation lists as able to block, when its purpose is to block. The enum holds only the event a shipped hook has actually used — an event admitted here without a hook occupying it would be a claim about harness behaviour nothing has exercised, which specs/0008's sourcing rule refuses.

matcher.description: Which tool invocations select this hook. It narrows what the hook is asked about and never substitutes for the hook's own check: specs/0010 R9 requires the hook to re-validate, because a matcher can select it on input the filter was written to exclude.

timeout.description: specs/0010 R11: stated rather than inherited. Bounded below 600 because that is the default the requirement exists to displace — a hook allowed to declare it would be inheriting it by hand.

guarantee.description: The single thing this hook enforces, with the requirement it comes from. specs/0006 R7 keeps it to one so a denial names a single condition and the hook can be retired without taking another guarantee with it.
